title: I Turned Leftover Bean Juice Into Vegan Meringues
summary: This BuzzFeed Nifty video demonstrates making vegan meringues from aquafaba, the liquid from canned chickpeas. The presenter cites Alton Brown as the recipe source, whips the aquafaba with cream of tartar and sugar, then pipes the foam into meringue shapes using a parchment-tube method before baking at a low temperature for about 90 minutes. The transcript also notes the etymology of aquafaba (Latin roots aqua and faba) and describes the resulting meringues as a crisp, sugar-cloud texture with a pleasant crunch, providing both practical steps and light culinary science around aquafaba as an egg-white substitute.

sections.title: Intro and aquafaba basics
sections.description: Opening discussion introduces aquafaba as a vegan alternative to egg whites, credits Alton Brown for the recipe concept, and notes using about 3/4 cup aquafaba.

sections.title: Whipping and stabilizers
sections.description: Cream of tartar is added to aquafaba as a stabilizer before whipping the liquid into a foam.

sections.title: Sweetening and peaks
sections.description: A half cup of sugar is added with vanilla, followed by whipping on high until the aquafaba forms stiff peaks.

sections.title: Shaping meringues
sections.description: A piping tube is fashioned from parchment paper and used to pipe the meringues.

sections.title: Oven prep and bake
sections.description: The oven is preheated to 200 degrees and the meringues are baked for about an hour and a half.

sections.title: Taste and closure
sections.description: Tasting commentary describes the result as a light, sweet, crunchy sugar-cloud with positive flavor and texture feedback.
